div.head: Ine 53.1
div.ab: Gif he þonne wite, hwá ðæs deadan yrfe hæbbe, tyme ðonne to þam yrfe ⁊ bidde ða hond þe þæt yrfe hafeþ, ðæt he him gedó ðone ceap unbesacene oþþe gecyþe, ðæt se deada næfre þæt yrfe ahte.
Gif he þonne wite, hwa ðæs deadan ierfe hæbbe, tieme þonne to þam ierfe ⁊ bidde ða hand þe þæt ierfe hafað, þæt he him gedó þone ceap unbeceasne oððe gecyðe, þæt se deada næfre þæt ierfe ahte.
Si tunc sciat, quis mortui pecuniam hereditauit, appellet in ipsam pecuniam et roget ipsam manum, ut hoc captale quietum ei faciat uel ostendat, quod nunquam ipsius mortui pecunia fuerit.
Gif he þonne wite hwa ðæs deadan ierfe hæbbe, tieme þonne to þam ierfe ⁊ bidde ða hond þe þæt ierfe hafað, þæt he him gedó þone ceap unbeceasne oþþe gecyðe, þæt se deada næfre þæt ierfe ahte.

If he, however, knows who owns the dead man’s inheritance, let him then vouch the estate to warranty and request of the man [hand] that has the inheritance, that he grant him the property uncontested or declare that the dead man never owned [that property as part of] the inheritance.

If, however, he knows who has succeeded to the estate of the dead man, he shall vouch the estate to warranty, and demand of the man who holds the estate that he shall make [his title to] the chattel incontestable, or declare that the dead man never owned the property.

If, however, he knows who has the dead man’s inheritance, he is then to vouch the inheritance to warranty, and ask the person that has the inheritance to make that purchase 1 incontestable, or to declare that the dead man never owned that property.

Wenn er jedoch weiss, wer des Todten Erbnachlass besitzt, dann ziehe er [die Gewähr] auf diesen Erbnachlass und fordere die Hand, die den Erbnachlass besitzt, auf, dass er [der Erbe] ihm [entweder] den Kaufgegenstand unbestritten mache oder beweise, dass jener Todte niemals diese Fahrhabe besessen habe.

But if he knows who possesses the dead man’s estate, then let him vouch [to warranty] upon that estate and call upon the hand that possesses the estate, that he [the heir] either make the purchased item undisputed for him or prove that the dead man never possessed that property.
